subject: HealthSync evaluation: success criteria & exit gates
messages:
From: Carl Meyer <carl@healthsync.com>
To: mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-05-17T16:10:00-04:00
Subject: Defining success metrics & exit gates for HealthSync eval

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with Redwood's streaming and the cost controls. We're ready to move into a short evaluation and want to lock down a Mutual Action Plan that clearly defines our acceptance tests and exit gates. High-level asks: 

- Primary success metrics: inference latency at 99th pct (p99) under load, semantic accuracy on our clinical note summarization set, and end-to-end availability during the trial window.
- Exit gates: pass/fail thresholds for each metric, a rollback plan if regressions occur, and signoff responsibilities.
- Timeline: 3-week evaluation window starting June 1, debrief + signoff by June 25.

We have two people on our side coordinating: me (Carl Meyer, Product) and Emily Zhang (Data Ops). Can you share a suggested set of acceptance tests (smoke + regression), who on Redwood will own them, and any required artifacts (sample dataset, runbook, dashboards)?

Also attaching our internal SOW draft for reference — it's in another email from procurement.

Best,
Carl Meyer
Product Lead, HealthSync

--

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-05-18T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Defining success metrics & exit gates for HealthSync eval

Hi Carl — thanks for the clear outline. Happy to own the MAP and make the acceptance criteria explicit. Draft MAP highlights below (attached XSLX):

1) Evaluation scope & timeline
   - Pilot window: 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-21 (21 days)
   - Two milestones: initial smoke (day 3), full-run conformance (day 18)

2) Acceptance tests (how we'll measure pass/fail)
   - Latency (p99) under production-like concurrency: < 450ms for 95% of requests, p99 < 900ms. Failure if p99 > 1200ms for 3 consecutive days.
   - Semantic accuracy: macro-F1 >= 0.78 on HealthSync holdout summarization set. Score computed nightly; regression of > 3 points triggers investigation.
   - Stability: sustained availability >= 99.5% during trial; incidents that cause > 5% error rate for > 30 minutes are considered blocking.

3) Test harness & artifacts required from HealthSync
   - 2k de‑identified clinical notes for the holdout set (format: ndjson with id,text,label).
   - Expected QPS/sequence-length distribution sample.

4) Runbook & rollback conditions
   - If any gate fails, automatic rollback to previously validated model variant; Redwood will notify stakeholders and remediate within SLA window.

5) Owners and communication cadence
   - Redwood test owner: Marissa Cole (QA lead) — will own daily smoke reports.
   - Redwood infra owner: Ben Carter — will own traffic shaping and bucketed canaries.
   - HealthSync data owner: Emily Zhang — provides dataset and labeling clarifications.

Next steps I propose: short 30-min workshop to review the proposed acceptance tests and confirm the dataset delivery timeline (I attached a spreadsheet that enumerates the tests and measurable thresholds). If that works we'll lock the MAP and produce a nightly dashboard link for the trial.

Attaching: proposed_map_v1.xlsx (contains test matrix and owners).

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Defining success metrics & exit gates for HealthSync eval

Looping in tactical details from the QA side. A few clarifications and additions to Mina's draft: 

- Smoke tests (day 0–3): API connectivity, tokenization sanity checks, KV cache warmup validation, single-batch correctness on 50 sample notes. Report format: CSV with id,pred,label,similarity_score.
- Conformance suite (day 10–18): 500-case random sample run nightly; we will publish nightly deltas and a final runbook artifact.
- Regression detection: we will compute BLEU/ROUGE and a healthcare-focused F1; primary metric for signoff remains the macro-F1 Mina listed.
- Observability: I'll create a per-model dashboard in the Redwood Console (token-cost, p99, error-rate, tail-latency heatmap). Please confirm who should receive the daily digest (Slack/email).

Action items assigned:
- Marissa Cole: QA dashboard + nightly digest (owner)
- Ben Carter: Canary traffic config and capacity reservation (owner)
- Emily Zhang: deliver holdout dataset and QPS profile by 2026-05-26

I'll block 30 minutes on Friday to walk through the runbook and the dashboard; Mina — can you confirm the calendar invite?

Thanks,
Marissa
QA Lead, Redwood Inference

- Can you call out the exact alerting thresholds (e.g., p99 > X triggers alert to HealthSync on-call) so procurement can reference them in the SOW?

Attaching SOW for procurement workflow (will follow up with DocuSign link). Looking forward to the walkthrough on Friday — calendar invite accepted.
